title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
spaceBreakdown:
- int j, int i: scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion → O(1)
- not counted: input vector nums (modified in place)
approach: Use a write pointer `j` marking where the next kept element goes. Scan with `i`; since the array is sorted, all duplicates of `nums[i]` are contiguous, so we only need to check whether `nums[i]` equals `nums[j-2]` (the element two slots before the write head). If `j < 2` (always keep the first two) or they differ, write `nums[i]` at `nums[j]` and advance `j`. This guarantees no value appears more than twice while preserving order in O(1) extra space.
hints: The array is sorted in non-decreasing order, so equal values sit next to each other. When you scan left to right and decide whether to keep the current element, what single earlier position would tell you that this value has already been kept twice?
Use a read pointer `i` and a write pointer `j`. On `nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3]`, after writing the first two 1s we have `j=2`; at `i=2`, `nums[i]=1` equals `nums[j-2]=nums[0]=1`, so we skip it.

```
j = 0
for i in 0..n-1:
    if j < 2 or nums[i] != nums[j-2]:
        nums[j] = nums[i]
        j = j + 1
return j
```

**Smallest input** - only one element, nothing to deduplicate.
`Input: nums = [5]` → `Expected: 1, nums = [5]`
⚠️ Bug: starting `j` at 1 instead of 0 → returns 1 but leaves `nums[0]` uninitialised/old, failing the value check.

**All elements equal** - every value would exceed the limit of two.
`Input: nums = [4,4,4,4,4]` → `Expected: 2, nums = [4,4,_,_,_]`
⚠️ Bug: comparing `nums[i] != nums[j-1]` instead of `nums[j-2]` → keeps only one 4, returns 1.

**Negatives and zeros** - values cross zero; comparison must still work.
`Input: nums = [-3,-3,-2,-2,-2,-1,0,0,0]` → `Expected: 7, nums = [-3,-3,-2,-2,-1,0,0,_,_]`
⚠️ Bug: using `<=` in the dedup check `nums[i] <= nums[j-2]` → skips `-2` at `i=3` because `-2 <= -2`, returns 6.

**Boundary at the start** - `j-2` is invalid before two writes have happened.
`Input: nums = [1,1,2]` → `Expected: 3, nums = [1,1,2]`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the `j < 2` guard and reading `nums[j-2]` when `j=0` → undefined behaviour / wrong skip of the first element.

followUps.q: Generalize so each value may appear at most `m` times.
followUps.a: Replace the `j < 2` guard with `j < m` and the check `nums[i] != nums[j-2]` with `nums[i] != nums[j-m]`. The write pointer still advances only when the element is allowed. Time stays O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if the input array is NOT sorted?
followUps.a: The `nums[j-2]` check no longer works because duplicates are not contiguous. You would need to count occurrences per value (e.g., a hash map), then overwrite in a second pass, costing O(n) time and O(n) space.

followUps.q: Process the array as a forward-only stream with O(1) memory and emit each kept element.
followUps.a: Keep the last two emitted values in two scalar variables instead of indexing `nums[j-2]`. For each incoming element, emit it unless it equals both of the last two emitted values. Time O(n), space O(1), and it never needs random access to the input.
